controls.title: Build practical security awareness
controls.statement: Provide recurring security awareness for employees, managers, executives and contractors, updated for current threats, system changes and lessons from incidents.
controls.risk: People could expose information or enable an attack because they do not recognise threats or understand the safe action to take.
controls.scope: Personnel and third parties who use organisational information, systems or services.
controls.examine: Review awareness objectives, audience coverage, content, completion, delivery dates, incident lessons and effectiveness measures.
controls.interview: Ask personnel how they recognise and report common threats and ask program owners how content changes when risk changes.
controls.test: Sample personnel across roles and verify timely participation and practical understanding using an approved exercise or scenario.
test_steps: Select personnel across locations, employment types and access levels, including recent starters and people who missed the original training window.
Verify assignment, completion and refresher dates against the required schedule and independently confirm that completion records belong to the sampled people.
Run an approved scenario or knowledge check covering reporting, phishing, credential handling and sensitive information, measuring actions as well as answers.
Compare weak results with targeted follow-up, repeat testing and trend reports to confirm the program changes when people do not demonstrate the expected behaviour.
controls.expected: The intended audience completes current awareness activities and can identify and respond to relevant security situations.

mappings.basis: Requires a security-awareness program with at least annual maintenance.
Requires initial and recurring literacy training and awareness, content updates and incident lessons.
Requires cybersecurity awareness activities to occur.
Requires periodic and trigger-based evaluation and improvement of awareness effectiveness.
Calls for specific, regular training for staff and contractors with access to critical sites and systems and says general IT-focused training is insufficient.

controls.title: Train people for their security responsibilities
controls.statement: Provide role-based training before people perform security-sensitive duties and refresh it for changes, incidents and evolving responsibilities.
controls.risk: People in sensitive roles could make unsafe decisions or respond poorly because general awareness does not teach the skills their duties require.
controls.scope: Personnel with security, administration, development, incident, privacy, physical-security or OT responsibilities.
controls.examine: Map roles and assigned responsibilities to training requirements, prerequisite completion, refresh cycles and assessed capability.
controls.interview: Ask role owners and participants how training prepares them for actual decisions, tools and incident scenarios.
controls.test: Sample sensitive roles and verify required training preceded access or duties and remains current after relevant changes.
test_steps: Identify roles with security-specific duties and select people who recently entered or changed those roles, including administrators, developers, responders and executives.
Compare role requirements with assigned training, completion dates, access activation and material process or technology changes.
Use a role-specific practical scenario to ask each sampled person to perform or explain a critical duty, escalation and prohibited action.
Confirm gaps lead to restricted duties or access, assigned remediation and a successful reassessment before independent work resumes.
controls.expected: People receive timely training matched to their responsibilities and can demonstrate the knowledge needed to perform them safely.

mappings.basis: Requires role-specific security awareness and skills training.
Requires role-based training before access or duties, periodically and when systems change.
Requires cybersecurity awareness activities to be tailored to job role.
Requires cybersecurity training before access to assets important to the function.
Requires workforce development and security material to be updated after incidents or environmental changes and promptly communicated.
